messages:
ana-m: Heads-up — proposing a weekend mirrored-traffic soak (Sat 0200-1200 UTC). Goal: run ~6hr soak with mirrored egress from prod to a shadow cluster to validate batching + kv-cache behavior under sustained load. Thinking k6 for traffic fidelity and locust for longer multi-worker soak. Thoughts?

devin: +1. Outline the core checks we need (regressions to watch for): p50/p95/p99 token latency, tail CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, request error spike, and memory growth. Also need a canary step first (~15m) before full mirror.

ana-m: typo — that's me ;) Can we mirror only a % of traffic first? e.g., header-based sampling 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3 steps. Also need to confirm no PII escapes to shadow cluster: payload strip or redact.

devin: Yep. Plan: header X-Redwood-Shadow:1 + sampling on router. Staging config already supports X-Shadow sampling. We'll push routing change with gradual ramp. Add redaction middleware (existing lambda) to strip user.email / user_id.

sara: Infra note: the shadow cluster will be in same region (us-east-1) to avoid cross-region noise. We have a GPU pool with reserved capacity for weekend. Need list of models + variants we should run — heavy ones (gpt-large-q8, redwood-v2-std) + a lightweight baseline for comparison.

kai: I'll own the k6 script updates. For fidelity I want to replay real request size distributions and sequence lengths. Will sample production logs and synthesize sessions. For soak we should disable prefix caching to test cold-path too (maybe a separate run).

ana-m: Good call. Let's keep two runs: 1) mirroring with normal cache behavior, 2) mirroring with prefix cache disabled (shorter warmup but stresses KV).

devin: k6 snippet for the ramp plan (put this in repo under infra/loadtests):

    import http from 'k6/http';
    import { sleep } from 'k6';

    export let options = {
      stages: [
        { duration: '10m', target: 50 }, // canary
        { duration: '20m', target: 250 },
        { duration: '5h', target: 500 }
      ],
      thresholds: { 'http_req_duration': ['p(95)<800'] }
    };

    export default function () {
      let headers = { 'X-Redwood-Shadow': '1' }
      http.post('https://api.shadow.redwood.local/generate', JSON.stringify({ /* payload */ }), { headers });
      sleep(1);
    }

kai: For locust: I'll run a separate 12hr worker cluster that focuses on sustained concurrency and slow memory leak detection. Locust can also run user-behavior sequences easily.

sara: Ops checklist for Saturday:
- open security exception for shadow ingress (team:net)
- allocate 6x A10 reserved GPUs to shadow cluster
- short-lived logging retention (7d) to avoid costs
- ensure observability ingest has the right tags (shadow:true)

ana-m: Monitoring / alerts? I want auto-alert on: >3% 5xx spike, p99 increase >2x baseline, GPU mem > 90% for >5m. If any triggers, automated ramp-down to 25% or full stop.

devin: We'll configure a rollout policy: canary -> ramp -> steady. Rollback triggers tied to the alerts you listed. Also I'll add a tracing sampling policy (10% for shadow) to keep span storage reasonable.

kai: Quick ask: who can approve the prod log sample I need? I need anonymized session traces for 24h (1M requests sample).

devin: I can sign off on the sample. Make sure SRE scrub script runs before export. Use /infra/logs/export with redact=true flag.

ana-m: Can someone volunteer to run the canary at 02:00 UTC and watch dashboards for the first 20m? Need eyes on p99, error rate, and opentracing calls.

kai: I'll do the canary watch. I'll post a quick checklist on #eng-oncall and bring up a zoom if anything odd.

sara: I'll coordinate resource allocation and add firewall rules. Will post confirmations by Fri 18:00 UTC.

devin: Once canary green, run the 3-step ramp script (we'll automate with the deploy bot). If anything fails we fallback to header X-Redwood-Shadow:0 (instant stop).

loadbot: [automated] Job scheduled: soak-mirror-1764127890; canary 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z -> full 6h. Run id: soak-1764127890.

ana-m: Pre-run docs to attach: link to k6 script (repo), redaction script, perf dashboard (Grafana link), triage runbook. I'll assemble in a single PR.

devin: small perf-regression checklist for post-soak: compare p99 and cost per token vs baseline, look for tail stalls, inspect kernel-level GPU stalls, and check batch size distributions.

kai: After soak, I'll run a focused locust memory/leak profile. Expect 24-48h of analysis.

sara: Confirmed infra prep done by Fri 18:00 UTC. I'll ping here when completed. :thumbsup:

ana-m: thanks all. tagging @kai @devin @sara for visibility. :eyes:

loadbot: [automated] Reminder: canary in 30m for soak-1764127890.

kai: canary started — monitoring p99, error, and GPU mem.

devin: canary looks clean at +12m. GPU mem stable, p99 within 1.1x baseline. Proceeding to ramp to 25%.

ana-m: proceeding to full soak in 40m unless any objections.

sara: no objections, infra ready.

loadbot: [automated] Ramp completed to 100% mirror. Soak running.

kai: noticing higher-than-expected KV miss-rate on one shard (shard-3). Opening an issue: https://stash.redwood.local/infra/issues/456

devin: thanks — will fallback that shard to cold-path routing and notify ops.

ana-m: Good catch. Keep notes for postmortem.

loadbot: [automated] Soak run summary (interim, 3h): 5xx spike 0.9%, p99 +1.4x baseline, KV hit-rate down 6% on shard-3. No OOMs.

kai: continuing to collect logs. Will upload session traces to shared bucket when done.

sara: all resource metrics stable otherwise. Will post final infra summary after run completes.

devin: thanks everyone. Post-soak follow-ups: create a regression ticket if p99 >1.2x or 5xx >1%.

ana-m: excellent. I'll draft the run notes and file follow-ups. :rocket:
